title: extcap for etw
description: This change creates a new extcap for etw. It converts etw events from a etl file to pcapng format and dump to the FIFO destination.

Hi,
Wireshark is a cross platform program and we want features to work on all platforms. As
far as I can see there is no reason to make this code windows only.

Hi,@AndersBroman, ETW (Event Tracing for Windows) is a way to instrument windows application only. The instrumented events are captured and saved in etl file. The etl file format is not public (not like pcapng) so it can be opened and processed only through APIs. All those APIs only work on Windows. So it is almost impossible to make etl_to_pcapng works on Linux. Once the etl is converted to pcapng on Windows, the converted pcagng file can be opened on Linux. Here is the MSDN reference for more details about ETW - https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/etw/event-tracing-portal.

I believe this merge request provides a way that extends Wireshark to dissect other providers in addition to MBIM provider. For example, Windows used to have a very popular application NetMon can decode IP packets from ETL file, Wireshark can be extended to do so after this merge request is approved. Because of that, I think it can inspire more windows developers to contribute to Wireshark.
Ok, my bad I missunderstod how it works.

> The etl file format is not public (not like pcapng) so it can be opened and processed only through APIs.

The second part of that statement does not follow as a consequence of the first part.  Wireshark reads *several* file formats that are not public; the formats have been reverse-engineered.

There is [a change on the old Gerrit code review site](https://code.wireshark.org/review/#/c/34431/) that has code to read ETL files.  The one issue with that change is that, according to the author, records in ETL files are not guaranteed to be in order, and the only way to get a time-ordered sequence of ETL records is to read the entire file and sort them.  Wireshark's APIs don't currently provide a way to handle files where the "open" process could take a long time, as would be the case here - the "open" phase would have to read all the records and sort them, and the "read" phase would read them in order by time rather than by position in the file.

*If* the file consists of batches of records, with a guarantee that 1) a batch is somewhat limited in size and 2) for all values of *N*, all the records in batch *N*+1 are guaranteed to be after all the records in batch *N*, we could handle that.  Otherwise, we might have to add a way for the file open operation to provide progress callbacks, so that there's an indication that Wireshark is doing work while opening an ETL file and sorting its records.

It is good to know there was a similar request that means I am not the only one think it is really needed.

Rather than reverse-engineered, I personally think it should be implemented by invoking APIs provided by Microsoft. There are multiple reasons,

- If Microsoft changes the format, the implementation based on the reverse-engineering will be broken and need reverse-engineering again. It is not good for long term maintenance and its stability.
- Many events need load resource from dll to dissect the event data, it could be tremendous work to reverse-engineering whole ETW implementation. Microsoft has provided APIs to do so, reverse-engineering what Microsoft did is not necessary and not valuable. 
- The etl file is generated and collected on Windows, a developer will barely collect it on windows, then copy it and load it on Linux. I believe it is good enough as long as it works on Windows.
assigned to @crondaemon

> The etl file is generated and collected on Windows, a developer will barely collect it on windows, then copy it and load it on Linux. I believe it is good enough as long as it works on Windows.

If so, then why not just have a standalone Windows utility, independent of Wireshark, that reads ETL files and produces pcapng files?

There is a tool called etl2pcapng that is created by Microsoft team - https://github.com/microsoft/etl2pcapng/. But it is not very convenient to run a separate tool at first and then run Wireshark to display the events. I also contacted the owner of this tool internally and he aggreged it is a good idea that Wireshark can open etl directly.
So I personally think Wireshark can benefit from supporting etl natively also, more Windows developers will begin to contribute to Wireshark (not another separate standalone windows utility) and use it, it is a win-win solution for both Wireshark community and Windows developer.

This is similar to what I had in mind some years ago. My idea was to create an extcap that run an actual capture via MS api and produced an pcap file to feed wireshark.
I'd appreciate much more that MS published the specs, but taking that way it's just a waste of time imho. Then having an extcap for an actual capture and/or a change like this for file reading sounds good to me. Relying on APIs is the most promising long-term way.

Hi @wiresharkyyh,
I compiled the branch and had a quick look at the MR. I really appreciate the idea behind it, but I don't think this is the correct implementation.
Libwiretap is an actual file reading library. Adding a new format means giving wireshark the ability to read a new file format.
However your change isn't an actual format reader. Instead it's an hack to change an ETL file into pcapng. This doesn't give wireshark the ability to read ETL files. Libwiretap requires some primitives (open, seek, etc) to work. Instead you added a "if" condition based on the file extension, that really sounds like an exception. Libwiretap is made of rules, not exceptions.
I really don't want to sound rude, because I really appreciated your work, that goes in the direction I wanted to go (but didn't find enough time), but I don't think wiretap is the place for this kind of code.
Instead I would suggest you to create one (or 2) extcap(s), that are much less related to a rule-based code as libwiretap. Other extcaps play their own rule: ssh takes packets from a host, randpktdump generates packets itself and so on. Conversions are things that IMHO can play free in an extcap.

When I say 1 or 2 excaps I mean that you could have an extcap that can run a capture and convert to pcap (as far as I recall pcapng is not yet supported by extcap), and extcap that opens a file from the disk and converts it, or a single multi-purpose extcap that can serve both.

Other core-devs, please integrate if you see the things in another perspective.

Of course the dissectors are out of this scope. They need to be reviewed separately.

@crondaemon,

I agree with you, I've been thinking about this for a while but hadn't gotten around to adding my comment.

I did discuss this with @rknall and he agreed that Wiretap is not the place for this, an extcap is better suited, especially as the conversion will only run on a Windows OS, so we can make the Windows build create the extcap and the Windows installer add it as an option.  Running as an extcap would also allow options to be set for the converted filename and path etc.

To me, as it seems that this is basically etl2pcapng, I would simply take the binary from that project (so they maintain the code) and run it from whatever extcap structure (python, C or C++ executable) you wish.

One issue with extcap is the lack of support for pcapng, so no support of multiple interfaces in the capture.
Just my 2 cents, extcap is capable of doing pacing. That issue got resolved some time ago.
Right, I didn't observe any issue when using pcapng in extcap so far.

Anyway, looks like extcap doesn't support pcapng, so sounds to me it cannot suit the needs well since it is very common that IP packet dissection (most etl contains multiple interfaces, like Wi-Fi, Ethernet) needs multiple interfaces.

- I can add new corresponding WTAP_FILE_TYPE_SUBTYPE_ETL, and add etl_open, etl_read and etl_seek_read in etl.c, and convert the etl to pcapng in etl_open, all funtions will be a wrapper of pcapng_open, pcapng_read, pcapng_seek_read. It is still a hack but with all Wiretap primitives.

+=begin man
+
+=encoding utf8
+
+=end man
+
+=head1 NAME
+
+etwdump - Provide an interface to read ETW
+
+=head1 SYNOPSIS
+
+B<etwdump>
+S<[ B<--help> ]>
+S<[ B<--version> ]>
+S<[ B<--extcap-interfaces> ]>
+S<[ B<--extcap-dlts> ]>
+S<[ B<--extcap-interface>=E<lt>interfaceE<gt> ]>
+S<[ B<--extcap-config> ]>
+S<[ B<--capture> ]>
+S<[ B<--fifo>=E<lt>path to file or pipeE<gt> ]>
+S<[ B<--iue>=E<lt>Should undecidable events be includedE<gt> ]>
+S<[ B<--etlfile>=E<lt>etl fileE<gt> ]>
+
+=head1 DESCRIPTION
+
+B<etwdump> is a extcap tool that provides access to a etl file.
+It is only used to display event trace on Windows.
+
+=head1 OPTIONS
+
+=over 4
+
+=item --help
+
+Print program arguments.
+
+=item --version
+
+Print program version.
+
+=item --extcap-interfaces
+
+List available interfaces.
+
+=item --extcap-interface=E<lt>interfaceE<gt>
+
+Use specified interfaces.
+
+=item --extcap-dlts
+
+List DLTs of specified interface.
+
+=item --extcap-config
+
+List configuration options of specified interface.
+
+=item --capture
+
+Start capturing from specified interface save saved it in place specified by --fifo.
+
+=item --fifo=E<lt>path to file or pipeE<gt>
+
+Save captured packet to file or send it through pipe.
+
+=item --iue=E<lt>Should undecidable events be includedE<gt>
+
+Choose if the undecidable event is included.
+
+=item --etlfile=E<lt>Etl fileE<gt>
+
+Select etl file to display in Wireshark.
+
+=back
+
+=head1 EXAMPLES
+
+To see program arguments:
+
+    etwdump --help
+
+To see program version:
+
+    etwdump --version
+
+To see interfaces:
+
+    etwdump --extcap-interfaces
+
+  Example output:
+    interface {value=etwdump}{display=ETW reader}
+
+To see interface DLTs:
+
+    etwdump --extcap-interface=etwdump --extcap-dlts
+
+  Example output:
+    dlt {number=1}{name=etwdump}{display=DLT_ETW}
+
+To see interface configuration options:
+
+    etwdump --extcap-interface=etwdump --extcap-config
+
+  Example output:
+    arg {number=0}{call=--iue}{display=Should undecidable events be included}{type=boolflag}{default=false}{tooltip=Choose if the undecidable event is included}{group=Capture}
+    arg {number=1}{call=--etlfile}{display=etl file}{type=fileselect}{tooltip=Select etl file to display in Wireshark}{required=true}{group=Capture}
+
+To capture:
+
+    etwdump --extcap-interface=etwdump --fifo=/tmp/etw.pcapng --capture
+
+NOTE: To stop capturing CTRL+C/kill/terminate application.
+
+=head1 SEE ALSO
+
+wireshark(1), tshark(1), dumpcap(1), extcap(4)
+
+=head1 NOTES
+
+B<etwdump> is part of the B<Wireshark> distribution.  The latest version
+of B<Wireshark> can be found at L<https://www.wireshark.org>.
+
+HTML versions of the Wireshark project man pages are available at:
+L<https://www.wireshark.org/docs/man-pages>.
+
+=head1 AUTHORS
+
+  Original Author
+  ---------------
+  Odysseus Yang             L<wiresharkyyh@outlook.com>

commits_data.title: ETW: Add a new extcap for reading events from an etl logfile
commits_data.message:
ETW: Add a new extcap for reading events from an etl logfile

This change add a new extcap to read the events from an etl logfile, convert
them to the DLT_ETW packets and dump the DLT_ETW packets to FIFO destination.

commits_data.title: ETW: Add a dissector to decode the header of DLT_ETW
commits_data.message:
ETW: Add a dissector to decode the header of DLT_ETW

This change add a new ETW dissector to display the header, the common message
and the provider name of a DLT_ETW packet. If the provider matches the MBIM
provider GUID, the MBIM dissector will be called to display a MBIM message.

commits_data.title: MBIM: Update dissector to support DLT_ETW
commits_data.message:
MBIM: Update dissector to support DLT_ETW

New link type DLT_ETW is added for write and read Event Trace on Windows.
This change updates MBIM dissector to decode a MBIM message from
a DLT_ETW packet.
